questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live and study in Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Sorbonne university is highly unclear in their communication.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a 3 hour presentation by many different people - some spoke french.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They gave us a student card but forgot to tell us how to activate it, so we couldn't buy lunch for the first two weeks. Also, the orientation happened after classes had already started. No social aspects.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in Cité Universitaire - the Fondation Danoise house

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire is the best student accommodation in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Highly confusing and complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Manual. I had to show up to various offices to get stamps of approval and send emails back and forth. In the end, I got access to a shared google sheet, where I could sign up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could schedule meetings with the academic advisor for the Erasmus students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had no problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always just go and talk to the academic advisor for the Erasmus students. Keep in mind that registration often happens during the semester, so it's normal to start courses before you are signed up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took M2 Fonda courses. They were quite difficult and meant as PhD prep.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Copenhagen is far more organised and easy to follow. Here it all depends on the specific lecturer. Some are good and some dont care.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Théorie de Lie, représentations et géométrie I, Groupes quantiques et algèbres amassées and various French language courses

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Groupes quantiques et algèbres amassées was interesting - we learned math developed within the last 10 years.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive. Wine was cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not participate.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire, where I lived, has a lot of stuff incl. a pool and a gym

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Bretagne or Normandie. Etretat on the coast is nice. Go see Monet's house and gardens in Giverny.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - people are nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in Cité Universitaire

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is much more bureacracy here and things are not digitalized.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Life in the city is so active and warm. Cafés and bars are lively.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient when it comes to getting signatures and signing up for courses. Things will work out, but it will seem frustrating. 
2. Learn some french before coming here and sign up for free french courses at Sorbonne
3. Apply to Cité Universitaire

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See the above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many wonderful people. Paris is beautiful city. Exploring it on pretty days is amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out the system at Sorbonne. Some of the courses were also highly confusing in the sense that we didn't really get exercises or material to study and the exams were not as expected - did not really match the things done in class.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Come here for the culture, the city, the wine, the people, the poetry and philosophy - it's inspiring. Don't come here for the academics.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
